methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a coherent in vitro design to test whether exosome-delivered miR-448 alters liver cancer cell phenotypes, with exosome isolation by ultracentrifugation and validation by TEM/NTA plus marker immunoblotting (CD63/CD9 with calnexin as negative control). It includes multiple mechanistic layers (RNase A +/- Triton protection assay for exosomal encapsulation; dual-luciferase assay for miR-448 binding to RAB7A 3'-UTR; and RAB7A knockdown/overexpression rescue experiments) and evaluates functional endpoints (CCK-8 proliferation; Transwell migration/invasion; glycolysis readouts including ECAR, lactate, glucose uptake, ATP). The main methodological limitation is scope: findings are based on cell-line experiments without in vivo validation or patient-derived samples, which the discussion also acknowledges. Statistical methods are standard (t-tests/ANOVA with Tukey, mean +/- SD from >=3 independent experiments), but there is no explicit multiplicity control across many endpoints and comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical, cell-line-based mechanistic study (exosomal miRNA effects on liver cancer cell behavior and glycolysis), which maps to Oxford LoE 5. The proposed axis (EXO-miR-448 targeting RAB7A to suppress malignant phenotypes and glycolysis) has plausible translational relevance for hepatocellular carcinoma biology and therapeutic development, but no patient outcomes, biomarker performance, or in vivo efficacy/toxicity are demonstrated in the manuscript. The authors explicitly note the limitation of exclusive in vitro assays and call for animal model validation.

reporting_quality.justification: No single canonical reporting checklist in the provided rubric cleanly fits an in vitro exosome/miRNA mechanistic study, so 'other' is most appropriate; within that constraint, the methods are described with substantial procedural detail (cell line provenance and mycoplasma testing; ultracentrifugation steps; RT-qPCR conditions; Seahorse ECAR protocol). However, several reproducibility elements are not clearly captured in the text excerpt (e.g., exact replicate numbers per assay beyond '>=3 independent experiments', and any preregistration or blinded outcome assessment). There is no statement describing deposition of raw data, processed data, or analysis code in a public repository.

novelty_literature.justification: The work presents a meaningful mechanistic extension by linking exosomal miR-448 to RAB7A and glycolytic suppression with functional rescue experiments, which goes beyond a purely correlative miRNA expression report. At the same time, the manuscript cites prior evidence that miR-448 can suppress HCC proliferation/glycolysis via other targets and that RAB7A is implicated in HCC metabolism, making the contribution incremental rather than first-in-class. Novelty is therefore best characterized as a solid extension/combination of known themes (exosomal miRNA regulation plus glycolysis via RAB7A) rather than a paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with well-separated methods subsections and a results narrative that follows the experimental logic from exosome validation through target identification and rescue. Quantitative/technical specifics are frequently included (e.g., ultracentrifugation at 100,000 x g; median exosome size around 104 nm; Seahorse injection sequence and concentrations), supporting interpretability. Figures are referenced consistently (e.g., Fig. 1-4) and limitations are explicitly stated in the discussion, though the absence of in vivo data necessarily limits the strength of the conclusions.

key_strengths: Methodologically coherent in vitro pipeline with multiple orthogonal validations of exosomes (TEM/NTA/markers) and mechanistic confirmation of the miR-448 to RAB7A link (luciferase plus knockdown/overexpression rescue).
Phenotype-to-mechanism alignment: proliferation/migration/invasion changes are paired with metabolic readouts (ECAR, lactate, glucose uptake, ATP) consistent with the glycolysis claim.
Reasonable cell-line rigor signals are reported (supplier STR authentication, <10 passages, PCR mycoplasma testing).
key_concerns: Exclusively in vitro evidence base with no animal or patient-derived validation, limiting translational claims about therapeutic potential.
Statistical approach is basic for a multi-endpoint study (t-tests/ANOVA without explicit multiplicity strategy), and replicate structure is only summarized as '>=3 independent experiments'.
No data/code sharing or repository deposition is described, constraining reproducibility.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a solid, incremental mechanistic study with good internal experimental logic and rescue experiments, but its purely in vitro scope and limited reproducibility posture make tier-3 acceptance plausible only after major revisions focused on validation and transparency.
